text:
maya: Hey — hitting a weird one on Android 11 emulator: after token refresh interceptor runs on a 401, the retried request loses the Authorization header sometimes. Repro fairly consistent on emulator only.

devin: Ugh. Is it the OkHttpAuthenticator flow or our custom interceptor?

maya: It's our Authenticator (implements okhttp3.Authenticator). Flow: 401 -> Authenticator does sync token refresh -> builds new request with header Authorization: Bearer <new-token> -> returns request. But server logs show the retried request sometimes missing the header.

arjun: Do you have a minimal repro? Could be connection pooling + header mutation race on the same connection.

maya: Repro steps: 1) app on Android 11 emulator image 30 2) hit protected endpoint with expired token 3) server responds 401 4) our Authenticator calls synchronous refresh endpoint 5) return request with new header. Happens ~30% of attempts.

maya: Snippet:```java
@Override
public Request authenticate(Route route, Response response) throws IOException {
  String newToken = tokenProvider.refreshSync();
  return response.request().newBuilder()
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer " + newToken)
    .build();
}
```

devin: That looks correct. Does tokenProvider.refreshSync() make network calls on the same OkHttpClient instance? If so, that can deadlock or reuse dispatcher threads.

maya: It uses a separate OkHttpClient (okHttpClientInternal) but same process. Logs show the refresh completes and response.request() used in returned request still has old header stripped.

arjun: Could be: when using connection: keep-alive + 100-continue? Or the proxy/interceptor chain has an earlier interceptor that removes headers for follow-up. Any network interceptors that mutate headers?

maya: We only add a network interceptor for telemetry that attaches x-client-id. No header stripping. Also this only happens on emulator API 30+ images. Real devices OK.

devin: Try forcing request().newBuilder().removeHeader("Authorization").addHeader("Authorization", ...) to be explicit. Also maybe mark the request as .tag(...) to differentiate?

maya: Tried removeHeader as well. No luck. But I noticed when I disable connection pooling (`new OkHttpClient.Builder().connectionPool(new ConnectionPool(0, 1, TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS))`) issue disappears.

arjun: That hints at connection-level state. OkHttp may reuse an existing call with prior headers on a multiplexed connection and the server ignoring new auth on subsequent stream? Which protocol? HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2?

maya: Emulator seems to prefer HTTP/1.1 in our setup. Server is http1.1.

devin: Could you try returning a completely new Request built from scratch (not response.request().newBuilder())? e.g., new Request.Builder().url(response.request().url()).method(response.request().method(), response.request().body()).header(...).build()

maya: I tried that: behavior improved but still occasional loss. However switching to perform refresh on a separate thread and enqueueing a new call instead of returning from Authenticator works reliably. Not ideal but suggests timing.

arjun: Emulator networking + host loopback can reorder packets; maybe the server's 401 connection is reused and our follow-up is being treated as a separate call without proper header propagation. Could also be a bug in platform's TLS stack on API 30 emulator images.

maya: Filed a small reproducer app and tested: native okhttp 4.9.3 on emulator image 30 shows the bug; on device and on emulator image 31 no issue.

devin: Action items: 1) Add a defensive workaround in our SDK: if Authenticator refresh occurs on emulator/API<=30, force new connection (Connection: close) or disable connection pooling for that call. 2) Add a note in DX docs about known emulator header-loss quirk. 3) Open an OkHttp/Android emulator issue with repro.

maya: I'll push a patch that does Connection: close as a header on the retried request when we detect emulator API 30. Patch short and marked with a TODO referencing this thread.

ci-bot: Build passed for branch fix/emulator-auth-header-30 (suite: unit, small integration). :white_check_mark:

devin: Nice. Please add a short e2e test that runs the reproducer on a cloud emulator matrix if possible, so we don't regress.

maya: Will do. Thanks for the quick debugging help :thanks:
